options: A table containing only the rows where the condition evaluated to true
A single scalar number
A Boolean TRUE or FALSE value
A new calculated column
questions.explain: Unlike a simple Boolean condition, FILTER returns an entire table — a filtered subset of rows from the table you pass it.

questions.q: In 'FILTER(<table>, <filter>)', what is the second argument?
options: A Boolean condition evaluated for every row of the table
The name of a column to remove
Another table to merge with the first
A sort order
questions.explain: The filter argument is a Boolean expression checked row by row — only rows where it's true make it into the returned table.

questions.q: Why does FILTER almost always appear nested inside another function like CALCULATE or SUMX?
options: Because FILTER returns a table, which needs to feed into something that can aggregate or use it — not display directly
Because FILTER can only be used inside calculated columns
Because FILTER is deprecated in favor of newer functions
Because FILTER requires a measure argument to work at all
questions.explain: A table isn't something a visual displays directly the way a single aggregated value is — FILTER's table result needs to be consumed by something like SUMX or CALCULATE.

questions.q: When should you reach for FILTER instead of a simple Boolean condition directly inside CALCULATE?
options: When the condition depends on a related table's column, combines multiple complex conditions, or compares against a calculated value
Always — FILTER should replace every simple Boolean condition
Only when working with DirectQuery data sources
Never — FILTER and Boolean conditions are functionally identical in every case
questions.explain: Simple, single-column conditions are better expressed directly. FILTER earns its place for related-table lookups, complex logic, or conditions comparing against computed values.

questions.q: In the NON USA Internet Sales example, what does RELATED do inside the FILTER condition?
options: Retrieves the country from the related SalesTerritory table for the current InternetSales row
Creates a new relationship between two tables
Removes a filter from the SalesTerritory table
Converts the FILTER result into a single number
questions.explain: RELATED pulls a value from a related table based on the current row's relationship — here, looking up each sale's territory country to filter by.
